Whether the Selected Developer Agreement between MISO and Transource was executed (due within 60 days of the Jan 6, 2026 report) was not confirmed in cached sources.

Application filing date conflict. The Dairyland page says 'In June 2024, Dairyland applied' and also 'CPCN application submitted in July 2024', and the cached application cover is dated July 2024. The PSC decision instead records the application as filed 2025-02-14, found complete 2025-03-17, with a revised version filed 2025-11-10. The cached sources do not explain how the July 2024 submission relates to the 2025-02-14 filing. The decision cites the application as PSC REF# 567118 ('page 21 of 270'), which does not match the 268-page July 2024 PDF; it is probably a later version that was not retrieved.

Decision date: the Final Decision is signed 'the 10th day of March, 2026', while the Dairyland page says the Written Order was issued March 11, 2026. The service date is not shown in the cached text, and the decision takes effect one day after service. The Commission deliberated at its 2026-02-05 open meeting; the page says the approval came in February 2026.

Western endpoint line ID is inconsistent. Decision pp.1, 5 and 13 say 'existing LQ-43 transmission line'; decision p.14 says 'LQ-34-4 transmission structure'; decision p.28 and the application say structure 'LQ-34-3' on Dairyland's LQ-34 line. 'LQ-43' looks like a transposition but this is not confirmed.
Decision p.13 spells the terminating station 'Tremval Nouth Substation' (typo), while pp.1 and 5 say 'Tremval North Substation'.

Decision segment labels are swapped. p.27 says the Southern Route's unique segment is 2B (Northern: 2A, 3, 4), but p.28 calls the Southern segment '2A' and the Northern one '2B'. The application uses 2B for the Southern Route.

Length and segment differences: the PSC says the South Route is about 35 miles; the Dairyland page and the July 2024 application say 34 miles. Segment 1A is 1.1 miles in the decision but 0.7 mile in the July 2024 application.

Exact location of the new Tremval North switching station is not in the cached sources or OSM. The decision's 0.7-mile Segment 6 running north and the name 'Tremval North' fit the application's northern option (about 0.5 mi NW of existing Tremval, north of the Trempealeau River). This should be confirmed in the WWTC final decision (5-CE-158).

WWTC docket numbers differ: the July 2024 application cites 'PSCW Docket No. 4220-CE-188' (Xcel), while the PSC decision cites joint NSPW/ATC docket 5-CE-158 (decided 2025-12-11). The xcel-wwtc researcher should confirm the mapping and whether ATC co-owns parts of WWTC.

Construction end is not stated by the PSC decision, which gives start Q4 2026 and in-service September 2028. Its vegetation-clearing window ends 'by the start of the 2nd quarter (April 1st)' without a year (probably 2027, but not stated).

The July 2024 application's schedule conflicts internally: its narrative says construction begins Q2 2026, but Southern Route Table 1.8-2 starts ROW staking and clearing in Q4 2026. It also assumed CPCN approval in Q3 2025, so the schedule is superseded.

Alma Substation is not named in OSM. Unnamed OSM power=substation way 160511826 (161/69 kV, 44.30956,-91.91088), where the 161 kV line to Tremval begins, is a probable but unconfirmed match. The western endpoint uses the application's Segment 1A coordinate instead.

Intermediate route vertices come from OSM way 258551045, an unnamed 161 kV Alma-Tremval line with no ref tag. The official Southern Route GIS shapefiles filed on PSC ERF (application section 1.10) and the Appendix A figures were not retrieved; either would allow an official-gis route.

Grid Forward: the cached sources do not say whether Grid Forward (5-CE-157) ends at the same new Tremval North switching station or at another Tremval facility, and they document no Dairyland-ATC coordination. ATC intervened in 1515-CE-103 but offered no evidence and filed no briefs.

Related Minnesota work under LRTP Project 4 is not modeled here: the Mankato-Mississippi River 345 kV project (MPUC E002/CN-22-532 and TL-23-157, filed 2024-04-02 by Xcel Energy, Dairyland, Rochester Public Utilities and SMMPA) and Dairyland's Wabasha Relocation Project (MPUC ET3/CN-23-504 and TL-23-388).

Dairyland page issues: the link text 'The Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity is available for viewing here' points to the July 2024 CPCN application PDF, not a certificate (the 'Written Order' link is the final decision). The page also calls the regulator the 'Public Utilities Commission of Wisconsin'.
The PSC final decision copy used here is hosted on dairylandpower.com. The regulator-hosted ERF copy (PSC REF#:582638) was not fetched, so the hashes cannot be cross-checked.

Status 'approved' rests on the CPCN approval and the page's 'PLANNING' label. No cached source confirms whether on-site construction or vegetation clearing had begun by 2026-09-26; the PSC expected construction to start in Q4 2026.
Cost claims differ by version: $188,796,752 (PSC, authorized South Route, excluding AFUDC) versus $177,383,646 (July 2024 application, Southern Route).

No PUCT docket was found for the SPS Texas segment as of 2026-09-26. Xcel lists a PUCT Certificate of Convenience and Necessity as required (xcel-potter-beckham-siting p.2), and routing and siting studies run through Q4 2026, so a CCN application is probably not yet filed. This was not confirmed on the PUCT Interchange.

No OCC cause number exists yet for the Oklahoma segment. Transource expects to file its Certificate of Authority application in summer 2027, with a decision in late 2027 (fact sheet graphic: 'FALL - WINTER 2027 OCC Approval').

No SPP Notification to Construct naming SPS or Transource Oklahoma for Beckham County-Potter was found. The Nov 4, 2025 minutes direct SPP staff to issue an NTC to the DTO. SPP-NTC-220936 (SPS, Oct 17, 2025, cached) covers Potter-Crossroads-Phantom 765 kV. It includes a 'Potter County 345 kV Substation Expansion' 'for the addition of three new 345 kV lines' (p.10), which are listed as Tecovas-Potter County circuits. Whether any Beckham line terminal work at Potter is included is not stated.

Whole-line length conflicts across sources: 125 mi (Xcel page and info sheet, Transource page, and 110 + 15 segment sums), ~128 mi (Nov 21, 2025 Xcel and Transource releases) and ~150 mi (SPP IEP report, Oct 14, 2025, PDF p.9). The segment lengths (110 mi TX, 15 mi OK) are consistent between utilities.

The SPP IEP report splits winning Proposal B into B-1 (89% of the project) and B-2 (11%) without naming them. The 89/11 split is consistent with SPS 110 mi / Transource 15 mi, but no source states the mapping.

The Texas-Oklahoma crossing point is undetermined: no final route in either state, and Transource's map shows several preliminary crossing links. The 'tx-ok-state-line' place is a county-edge placeholder (Beckham County's western boundary midpoint, +/-27 km), not a sourced point.

Season-to-date conversion for the Transource construction window is a convention, not a sourced fact: Spring 2028 = 2028-03-01..2028-06-20 and Late 2028 = 2028-09-01..2028-12-31. Under these bounds the construction windows overlap only as 'possible' (SPS starts Q3 2028; Transource ends late 2028). The overlap becomes 'confirmed' only if 'Late 2028' is read as starting after 2028-09-30.

Schedule gap: the Transource timeline shows Oklahoma construction ending late 2028 but in-service in late 2029. Xcel shows Texas construction running Q3 2028-Q4 2029 with in-service in Q4 2029. The sources do not explain the Oklahoma gap, and whole-line energization timing should not be inferred.

Not modeled as construction windows: Transource's 'EARLY 2028 Right-of-Way Acquisition' (a milestone with no end date), 'SPRING 2027 Final Line Route Determined', and 'FALL - WINTER 2027 OCC Approval'.

In-service claims agree in substance: Q4 2029 (Xcel TX), Late 2029 (Transource OK), November 2029 (both Nov 2025 releases) and a November 2029 schedule guarantee from both Proposal B respondents in the SPP IEP report. The IEP table also mentions 'November 12th, 2029', but that sits in Proposal A's column (NextEra), so it is not attributed to these packages.

The Beckham County substation is an existing OG&E facility, and OG&E is a third utility. No source documents OG&E terminal work or an OG&E package for this line. SPP-NTC-220965 (OG&E, Dec 19, 2025, cached) does not mention Beckham.

Resource sharing is unknown. Xcel's Nov 2025 release quotes an Xcel director saying the partnership combines 'expertise' and 'resources', but no source documents shared crews, equipment, procurement or joint construction scheduling. Coordination is recorded as known-joint / joint-initiative, not resource-sharing.

SPP's IEP report calls this line a 'necessary companion project' to SPS's Potter-Crossroads-Phantom 765 kV line, and both use the Potter County substation. That pairing has the same owner (SPS) and belongs in a separate cluster if the 765 kV project is added; it is not a cross-utility lead.

The Potter substation coordinate is the OSM facility 'Potter County Interchange' (345/230 kV, Xcel). A cross-check against Xcel's location ('approximately six miles northwest of the intersection of SH 335 and US 87') could not be finished because Overpass timed out. The Beckham County coordinate was cross-checked and matches (5.9 mi SE of the SH 152/SH 6 junction).

Transource's project web page shows its timeline as an SVG image with outlined text, which cannot be verified by script. It was viewed and matches the fact sheet PDF, so all Transource schedule excerpts cite the fact sheet.
The Xcel information sheet graphic says '(Schedule is subject to change.)', but that text is not in the cached text extraction, so it is not cited.
